scope: Corollary 1.3 of the manuscript “Short Egyptian fractions” (preprints/Short-Egyptian-fractions-September-25-2026/Short-Egyptian-fractions-September-25-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 025 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 25eebdc1f077f245), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 3. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every sufficiently large integer k, exp ( exp(k/600) ) ≤ v(k) ≤ 1 + k2k−1 . More precisely, log 2 257 ≤ lim inf k→∞ log log v(k) k ≤ lim sup k→∞ log log v(k) k ≤ log 2. Equivalently for the lower bound, every fixed c < log 2/257 satisfies v(k) ≥ exp(exp(ck)) for every sufficiently large integer k. In particular log log v(k) = Θ(k).
